segments.title: Groundwork for the new components and hooks
context: This change adds a Pokemon page at /pokemon and a link to it in the header of every page. The page lists the Pokemon from the API with their level and types, and a professor can narrow the list to one type or to the Pokemon of one trainer.

waypoints.title: Added `formatTypes()` to write the types of a Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `formatTypes()` that returns the primary type of a Pokemon, or both types joined by ` / ` when it has a second type, such as `water / flying`. [`<PokemonPage />` calls it for each Pokemon of the list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L17), so that each line shows the types after the name and the level.

waypoints.title: Modified `<RootLayout />` to link to the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the component `<RootLayout />` to render a `<Link to="/pokemon">` with the text `Pokemon` in the header, between `Trainers` and `Items`. [The route table renders `<PokemonPage />` at that path](code:src/router.tsx#L14), so that a professor can open the new page from every page.

waypoints.title: Added the shape of the filter store
waypoints.reading: The author added an interface `PokemonFiltersState` with the two filters, `type` and `trainerId`, each `null` when nothing is chosen, and the three actions that change them. [`create()` types the store with it](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L12), so that [`<PokemonFilters />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L9) and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L13-14) read typed values.

waypoints.title: Added the Zustand store of the Pokemon filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a Zustand store `usePokemonFilters` that:

- starts with no type and no trainer chosen
- sets the type with `setType()` and the trainer with `setTrainerId()`
- sets both back to `null` with `clear()`

[`<PokemonFilters />` writes the filters](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L9) and [`usePokemon()` reads them](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L13-14), with no import between the two, so that a pick in the filters changes the list the page shows.
waypoints.coreChange: This store is where the filters live. The filter component writes it and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) reads it, so what each filter starts at and what `clear()` sets decide what the page lists.

findings.title: `usePokemonFilters` keeps the filters after the page closes
findings.reading: [`create()` makes the store once, at the top of the module](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L12), outside every component. So the chosen type and trainer stay set when a professor opens another page and comes back to /pokemon. Should the page open with the filters the professor chose last, or with no filter?

waypoints.title: Added the list of Pokemon types
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_TYPES` that lists the 18 Pokemon types, from `"normal"` to `"fairy"`. [`<PokemonFilters />` renders one option per type](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L15-19), so that the type filter offers every type.

waypoints.title: Added the type of one Pokemon type
waypoints.reading: The author added a type `PokemonType` that is the union of the names in `POKEMON_TYPES`. [The filter store keeps the chosen type as one](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L5), so that the store holds only a type the list has.

waypoints.title: Added the `Pokemon` interface
waypoints.reading: The author added an interface `Pokemon` with an `id`, a `name`, a `level`, a `primary_type`, a `secondary_type` that is `null` for a Pokemon with one type, and a `trainer_id` that is `null` for a Pokemon with no trainer. The fields keep the snake_case names of the JSON the API returns, so that [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon) returns the response as it is.

waypoints.title: Added `fetchPokemon()` to request the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `fetchPokemon()` that sends a `GET` request to `/pokemon`, with `?trainer_id=` and the id when a trainer is chosen, and returns the Pokemon of the response. [`request()` puts `/api` in front of the path](code:src/api/client.ts#L14). [`usePokemon()` runs `fetchPokemon()` as its query function](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L17), so that the page loads only the Pokemon of the chosen trainer.

waypoints.title: Added the query key of the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_QUERY_KEY` that holds `["pokemon"]`. [`usePokemon()` adds the chosen trainer to it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L16), so that each trainer has its own cached list and a new trainer loads the list again.

waypoints.title: Added `hasType()` to match a Pokemon against the type filter
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `hasType()` that returns `true` when no type is chosen, or when the primary or the secondary type of the Pokemon is the chosen type. [The `select` function of `usePokemon()` calls it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L18), so that a Pokemon with two types shows under both of them.

waypoints.title: Added `usePokemon()` to load the Pokemon that match the filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a hook `usePokemon()` that:

- reads the chosen type and trainer from [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters)
- loads the Pokemon of the trainer with [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon), under a key that holds the trainer
- keeps the Pokemon of the chosen type in `select`, with [`hasType()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#hasType)

[`<PokemonPage />` calls it](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L6), so that the list follows both filters. The trainer filter goes to the API, and the type filter runs in the browser on the loaded list.
waypoints.coreChange: This is where the two filters reach the data: the trainer goes into the query key and the request, and the type filters the loaded list in `select`. The page, the filter component and the store all exist for it.

children.title: Added the read of the chosen type
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFilters()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) with a selector that returns `type`. The hook renders again when the type changes, and [`select` keeps the Pokemon of that type](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L18).

children.title: Added the read of the chosen trainer
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFilters()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) with a selector that returns `trainerId`. [The query key holds it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L16), and [the query function sends it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L17).

children.title: Added the query of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to `useQuery` with the key `["pokemon", trainerId]`, a query function that calls [`fetchPokemon(trainerId)`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon), and a `select` function that keeps the Pokemon for which [`hasType()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#hasType) returns `true`. A new trainer is a new key, so the query requests again. A new type only runs `select` again on the cached list.

findings.title: `usePokemon()` empties the list each time the trainer changes
findings.reading: [The query key holds `trainerId`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L16), so a new trainer starts a new query with no data. While it loads, `isPending` is `true` and `data` is `undefined`, so [the page shows `Loading the Pokemon…` and no list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L11-13). `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` from `@tanstack/react-query` keeps the last list on screen until the new one arrives, for one more option. The fix also imports `keepPreviousData` on [the first line of the file](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L1).

waypoints.title: Modified the route table to add the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the route table `router` to add a child route `pokemon` of the layout that renders [`<PokemonPage />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#PokemonPage). `src/main.tsx` passes this table to `<RouterProvider />`, so that the page opens at `/pokemon` inside [`<RootLayout />`](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#RootLayout), where [the header links to it](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#L11).

waypoints.title: Added the value of the Every options
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `EVERY` that holds `""`. [The type select](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L13-14) and [the trainer select](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L21-22) use it as the value of their first option, and their handlers turn it into `null`. So the store holds `null` for no filter, and never `""`.

waypoints.title: Added `<PokemonFilters />` to choose the filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a component `<PokemonFilters />` that:

- renders a select with `Every type` and one option per type of [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/types/pokemon.ts#POKEMON_TYPES)
- renders a select with `Every trainer` and one option per trainer from [`useTrainers()`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L6-8)
- renders a `Clear filters` button
- writes each choice to [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters)

[`<PokemonPage />` renders it above the list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L10), so that a professor can narrow the list.

children.title: Added the read of the filter store
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFilters()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) with no selector, which returns the whole store: `type`, `trainerId` and the three actions. [The type select shows `type`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L13), [the trainer select shows `trainerId`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L21), and the handlers call the actions.

children.title: Added the query of the trainers
children.reading: The author added a call to [`useTrainers()`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L6-8) that gives the loaded trainers, with `[]` until they arrive. [The trainer select renders one option per trainer](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L23-27), so the select offers only `Every trainer` while the trainers load.

findings.title: `<PokemonFilters />` hides a failed load of the trainers
findings.reading: [`useTrainers()` reports a failed request in `isError`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L7), and `<PokemonFilters />` reads only `data`, with `[]` in its place. So when the trainers do not load, [the trainer select offers `Every trainer` alone](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L21-28), and nothing tells the professor why. The fix reads `isError` here, and the trainer select then needs a message for it.
trace: [The trainer select renders `Every trainer` and no other option](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L21-28).
findings.solution: const { data: trainers = [], isError: hasTrainerError } = useTrainers()

children.title: Added the handler of the type select
children.reading: The author added an `onChange` handler that calls [`setType()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L15-17) with the picked type, or with `null` when the picked value is [`EVERY`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L6). [`usePokemon()` reads the type](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L13), so that the list keeps only that type.

children.title: Added one option per Pokemon type
children.reading: The author added a loop that renders one `<option>` per name of [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/types/pokemon.ts#POKEMON_TYPES), with the name as its value and as its text.

children.title: Added the handler of the trainer select
children.reading: The author added an `onChange` handler that calls [`setTrainerId()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L18-20) with `Number(event.target.value)`, or with `null` when the picked value is [`EVERY`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L6). [`usePokemon()` puts the trainer in its query key](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L16), so that the page requests the Pokemon of that trainer.

children.title: Added one option per trainer
children.reading: The author added a loop that renders one `<option>` per trainer, with the `id` as its value and the `name` as its text. [The handler of the select turns the value back into a number](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L21).

children.title: Added the button that clears the filters
children.reading: The author added a `<Button variant="ghost">` with the text `Clear filters` that calls [`clear()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L21-23) when clicked. Both selects show their `Every` option again, and the page lists every Pokemon.

waypoints.title: Added `<PokemonPage />` to list the Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a page component `<PokemonPage />` that:

- renders the heading `Pokemon` and [`<PokemonFilters />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#PokemonFilters)
- loads the Pokemon that match the filters with [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon)
- shows `Loading the Pokemon…` while they load, and `The Pokemon could not be loaded.` when the request fails
- renders one line per Pokemon with its name, its level and [its types](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes)

[The route table renders it at `/pokemon`](code:src/router.tsx#L14), and [the header links to it](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#L11), so that a professor can browse the Pokemon.

children.title: Added the query of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) that gives the filtered `pokemon` and the flags `isPending` and `isError`. [The three conditions below read them](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L11-13).

children.title: Added the loading message of the Pokemon list
children.reading:
The author added a condition that renders `

Loading the Pokemon…

` while the query is pending. [The filters stay above it](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L10), so a professor can change them while the list loads.

children.title: Added the error message of the Pokemon list
children.reading:
The author added a condition that renders `

The Pokemon could not be loaded.

` when the query fails, as it does when [`request()` throws an `ApiError`](code:src/api/client.ts#L18).

children.title: Added the list of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a condition that renders a `<ul>` once the Pokemon have loaded, with one `<li>` per Pokemon that shows its name, `Lv.` and its level, and the text of [`formatTypes()`](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes).

findings.title: `<PokemonPage />` renders an empty list when no Pokemon matches
findings.reading: When the trainer has no Pokemon, or none of them has the chosen type, [`select` returns `[]`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L18). `[]` is truthy, so the condition renders an empty `<ul>`, and the professor sees the filters with nothing under them. A message for an empty list says that the filters match nothing, for one more condition.
